findings.title: A cross-cell structured ANSWER cannot round-trip: the question's key is resolved from the TARGET cell's view, and the reference is validated in the TARGET cell's team scope
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/protocol.ts · the `cellwork_send` answer branch (`const view = foldCellMail(readCellMail(caller.workspace, targetCellId))` then `questionId = … asked?.question?.questionId ?? ""`), and the `teamId: target.teamId` stamping; packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · sendMany (`scopeToTeam(state, input.teamId)` → `validateReferences(envelope, scoped.messages)`)
findings.what: Probe P8: the parent captain's question to `cell-sub/captain` succeeds (row written into the sub cell's view); the sub captain's answer to `cell-parent/captain` is REFUSED with 'an answer must carry the question's non-empty `questionId`' — because the answer path resolves the answered question from `readCellMail(targetCellId)` = the PARENT's view, where the question row (cellId = sub) does not exist. Probe P8b passes the key EXPLICITLY and still fails: '`replyTo` names no message in this mailbox … `answerTo` names no message …' — because the answer row is scoped to `target.teamId` (the parent's team) while the question row was stamped with the SUB cell's team. Plain cross-cell messages work both ways (P8 control).
findings.why: §1 says any cell agent may ask any other cell agent, and §6 is the cross-cell mapping; a parent/sub-cell question is the canonical use (the sub-captain needs a decision). Today the question crosses but the answer is impossible in BOTH directions, so the structured relay — the wave's core capability — is same-cell only. The first refusal is also misleading (it blames a missing key instead of a visibility problem), which would send a model hunting the wrong cause.
findings.direction: Layer 1 (T4): resolve the answered question from the SENDER's own cell view (`caller.cell.cellId`) — or from the union of the sender's and target's views — instead of `targetCellId`; name the real problem when the row is not visible. Layer 2 (store, coordinate with T15's in-flight edit): `sendMany` validates references against ONE team's scope, but a cross-cell conversation's rows live in two different teams; either validate references against the workspace mailbox (the 'same folded mailbox' §4 I5 actually describes) or let the view pass the conversation's team. Layer 1 is cellwork-only; layer 2 needs the captain's routing decision. Add a cross-cell question/answer arm to mail-unified.test.ts — no shipped arm covers it.
findings.evidence: probes.ts P8 and P8b in output.log

findings.title: A seat's mail address is the session id AT SEND TIME, so a reseeded seat (or one addressed through the synthetic never-raised key) can never acknowledge its own mail nor answer its own question
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/protocol.ts · seatId/seatAddress and the inbox ack (`acknowledgeCellMail(..., { byId: caller.sessionId, byName: seat })`), plus `fromMemberId: caller.member`; the reseed writes a NEW handle onto the cell record (protocol-core.ts promoteAfterHandoff → startContinuableAgent; dispatch.ts `handleFor` comment)
findings.what: Probe P1: the cell record says the planner's session is CURRENT, and a row addressed to its PREVIOUS session (STALE) is returned by every inbox call with `acknowledged: 0` and ZERO read records — the store's ownership check compares `toId` (STALE) with `byId` (CURRENT) and silently refuses. P1b control (row addressed to CURRENT) acknowledges once and disappears. The same identity gap blocks answers: P2c (question addressed to STALE, answered after the reseed) and P2 (question addressed to the synthetic `seat:cell/name` key) are both refused with 'only a recipient of the question may answer it'. The reseed is a supported path (bounded compaction failure), and the old name-addressed log tolerated it.
findings.why: §6 requires 'seat-scoped unread/ack-once … PRESERVED'. The unread side is seat-scoped (name match), but the ack/answer side is session-scoped, so a legitimate lifecycle event (reseed) makes every earlier row permanently un-acknowledgeable and every open question unanswerable — the inbox re-delivers forever with no error and no way out. That is exactly the relay failure this wave exists to remove, reintroduced at the identity seam.
findings.direction: Use a STABLE seat key on the cellwork plane (e.g. `seat:<cellId>/<name>`) for `toId`/`fromMemberId` AND for the inbox's `byId`, so a reseed changes nothing; keep `unreadFor`'s name matching. Alternatively teach `acknowledgeCellMail` to resolve the ack identity per row from the seat name. Either way, surface the refusal (N1) instead of reporting `acknowledged: 0`. Local to the cell view; no store change needed.

findings.title: An ownership refusal during the inbox ack is invisible: `markRead` returns moved ids only, `acknowledgeCellMail` drops `refused`, and the tool reports `acknowledged: 0` with the same rows and no reason
findings.where: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/mail.ts · acknowledgeCellMail; packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · markRead (`acknowledge(...).moved`); protocol.ts · cellwork_inbox answer
findings.what: Probe P1: the seat sees its row returned, `acknowledged: 0`, and nothing else — no refusal, no reason. A stalled seat cannot tell that its ack was refused for identity reasons.
findings.why: A silent zero is indistinguishable from 'nothing to ack' from the model's side; it makes F2 undiagnosable in the field.
findings.direction: Return the refusal list (or a one-line reason) on the inbox answer; `AckResult.refused` already exists one layer down.
